event.title: The arms that first held you
event.body: Wren Brindle decides what kind of shelter to make around this new life. The rain leaves the courtyard smelling of rosemary. Your household has little money, but people can offer time and teaching. An unsettled shelter household: Wren Brindle (shelter guardian). Birth parent 1 · identity unrecorded: missing; Birth parent 2 · identity unrecorded: unknown. These people are not offered as living contacts. No secure roof yet; household support 25/100. Not currently enrolled; free schools open at six, and independent reading remains a choice. A winter seed sprouted beside your cradle, its roots pointing toward the burial ground. Your family will remember the sign; its meaning must be discovered through childhood.

locations.name: Hearthmere
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

institutions.name: Hearthmere Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Hearthmere Lantern Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Vesperhold
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Vesperhold Alder Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Vesperhold Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Vesperhold Lantern Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Reedcross
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

institutions.name: Reedcross Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Reedcross Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Thicket
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Lantern Thicket Glass Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Fallen Bell Tower
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: The Fallen Bell Tower Lantern Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Stormward Peaks
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Stormward Peaks Lantern Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Reedwaste
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Reedwaste Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Quay
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Lantern Quay Hearth Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Astral Stair
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Astral Stair Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Wayfarer Camp
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Wayfarer Camp Rowan Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Dawn Gate

institutions.name: Reedcross Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Reedcross Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Thicket
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

institutions.name: The Lantern Thicket Glass Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Fallen Bell Tower
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

institutions.name: The Fallen Bell Tower Lantern Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Stormward Peaks
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

institutions.name: The Stormward Peaks Lantern Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Reedwaste
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

institutions.name: The Reedwaste Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Quay
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

institutions.name: The Lantern Quay Hearth Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Astral Stair
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

institutions.name: The Astral Stair Wren Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Wayfarer Camp
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

institutions.name: The Wayfarer Camp Rowan Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Dawn Gate
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

institutions.name: The Dawn Gate Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Thornward Keep
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

institutions.name: The Thornward Keep Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Thornward Keep Hearth Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

institutions.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary Alder Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Hearthward Sanctuary Alder Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Vesperhold, necromancy is forbidden; in Hearthmere, it is regulated; in Reedcross, it is permitted. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Wild groves are protected as common ground, and moon watchers teach respect for changing seasons.

festival.name: The First Moon Fair
festival.tradition: Apprentices display their work beside the oldest local craft masters.

rumors: The academy in Vesperhold is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.

locations.name: Hearthmere
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

locations.name: Vesperhold
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. locations.name: Reedcross

locations.name: The Lantern Thicket

institutions.name: The Lantern Thicket Glass Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Fallen Bell Tower

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Vesperhold, necromancy is forbidden; in Hearthmere, it is regulated; in Reedcross, it is permitted. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.

event.title: A name missing from the reading room
event.body: An old book reaches the community reading room with a former owner’s name cut away. A patron offers to buy it, while a teacher asks you to help recover its history. Scholarship and ordinary work compete for the same attention. The rain leaves the courtyard smelling of rosemary. Last year, your choice to ask and investigate was remembered. locations.name: Hearthmere
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Vesperhold, necromancy is forbidden; in Hearthmere, it is regulated; in Reedcross, it is permitted. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.

event.title: A name missing from the reading room
event.body: An old book reaches the community reading room with a former owner’s name cut away. A patron offers to buy it, while a teacher asks you to help recover its history. Scholarship and ordinary work compete for the same attention. The rain leaves the courtyard smelling of rosemary. Last year, your choice to ask and investigate was remembered. Your household has little money, but people can offer time and teaching. An unsettled shelter household: Wren Brindle (shelter guardian). locations.name: Hearthmere
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

locations.name: Vesperhold
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

institutions.name: Vesperhold Alder Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Vesperhold Lantern Chapter

locations.name: Reedcross

institutions.name: Reedcross Wren Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Reedcross Alder Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Lantern Thicket

institutions.name: The Lantern Thicket Glass Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Fallen Bell Tower

institutions.name: The Fallen Bell Tower Lantern Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Vesperhold, necromancy is forbidden; in Hearthmere, it is regulated; in Reedcross, it is permitted. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.

Born in Hearthmere to a struggling household, you grew through three childhood moments into a unformed.

After 10950 adult days, at age 30, you chose a quieter life as a person still free to find a calling. Your ambition was “Protect the place I call home.”

The region’s fever remained part of the world you lived in. You gave 0 clinic shifts to its people.

You made a home in modest lodgings, developed your career to rank 0, and recorded 0 years of changing priorities.

Mira shared part of your road. At seven, you looked for the truth about the missing charm.

You kept 0 recorded promises. No unresolved local charge followed you into retirement.

locations.name: Wrenfield
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

locations.name: Goldmere
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

institutions.name: Goldmere Glass Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Goldmere Lantern Chapter

institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Cresswater Glass Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Greywood Lantern Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Saltbell Harbor Lantern Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Goldmere, necromancy is permitted; in Wrenfield, it is forbidden; in Cresswater, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
